title: fix(console): open a form action inside the app it was fired from
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuWWgDeTcfrMpniKurLbGeyX)_

Fixes #13433

A `type: 'form'` action fired inside an app now opens its form inside that app's shell, headed by a real label, with a Cancel.

## What was wrong

Clicking the showcase's **Log Time** on a task record (`type: 'form'`, `target: 'showcase_task.form'`) navigated to the app-less `/forms/showcase_task.form?recordId=…&recordObject=showcase_task`:

- the app's sidebar, switcher and branding disappeared, because `/forms/:name` is mounted outside every app and renders in `DefaultHomeLayout` (objectui#4109);
- the page was headed by the raw qualified view name, because `resolveInternalForm` fell back to the view name when the view carried no label (a container's default form never does);
- the only button was Submit, so the browser's Back button was the only way out without saving.

## What changed

**An in-app twin of the form route.** The console's app route table now also serves `/apps/:appName/forms/:name` (`InAppFormRoute`, in `InternalFormRoute.tsx`, mounted through a new `appRoutes` fragment in `AppContent.tsx`). It renders the same internal `FormPage`; `ConsoleLayout` and the app's `ExpressionProvider` are already around it, so the form gets the app's own sidebar and branding. A submit lands on the written record in the app the URL names.

**Which hops go there.** `hostInConsolePath` takes an optional third argument, `routeAppSegment`: the `:appName` of the caller's own app route. When it is given, a `/forms/...` hop becomes `/apps/APP/forms/...` with the query string and hash kept. Every other path is sorted exactly as before.

- `RecordDetailView` passes its route's `appName` (the card's path: record header, related and section actions).
- `useConsoleActionRuntime` takes a new optional `routeAppSegment` option. `ObjectView` (list toolbars) and `PageView` (page buttons) pass their route's app.
- The console-wide runtime in `ConsoleShell` sits above the route tree and passes nothing, so its form hops keep `/forms/:name`.

The app is never inferred. The navigators' existing `hostAppSegment` (the last app the shell published, else the first active one) is deliberately NOT used for forms, so a form fired from Home does not open in a guessed app. This is the design objectui#4280's ruling named as its reopen condition (comment 5299952645, 2026-08-15): a report of the missing navigation, together with a design that "carries app context on the route (an explicit app segment or equivalent) rather than guessing it". `/forms/:name` itself is unchanged and keeps serving cold deep links.

**The heading.** `resolveInternalForm` now reads the view label, then the form config's `title` (the order the public route already uses, objectui#8408), and no longer falls back to the view name. A form that names itself nowhere is headed by its object's label, resolved through the session's language at render (`objectLabel`). The public route's heading is unchanged.

**Cancel.** The internal form (both routes) has a Cancel next to Submit. It goes back when react-router has an entry behind this one (`location.key !== 'default'`), which keeps the record page's own URL state (tab, `?form=`). On a cold link it goes to the record being edited when `recordPath` names it, else to the route's `cancelPath`: the app's home in-app, `/home` on the app-less route. Cancel writes nothing. The public `/f/:slug` form has no Cancel.

Docs: `content/docs/guide/public-forms.md` (the console route section). Changeset: `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/console`, patch.

## Tests

- `FormPage.inAppShell-13433.test.tsx` (new): the heading (object label, authored `title`, and the view label still winning as a control), Cancel (back, cold edit, cold create, writes nothing, none on the public form as a control), and the in-app route (renders inside the URL's app; a submit from the second app lands in that app; Cancel on a cold create lands on the app's home).
- `RecordDetailView.onSuccessNavigateHost-13396.test.tsx`: a new describe for the form hop (hosted under the route's app with query and hash, the route's app beats the shell's published one, outside an app route it stays `/forms/...`, `/formsx/...` is not matched, and a real `type: 'form'` run through the page's runner). The `CONSOLE_ROOT_SEGMENTS` table test now leaves `forms` to that describe.
- `useConsoleActionRuntime.onSuccessNavigateHost-13379.test.tsx`: `routeAppSegment` hosts a form hop, beats the published app, moves no other console route, and drives a real `type: 'form'` run. Its existing "a `type: 'form'` action still opens `/forms/:name`" case (no `routeAppSegment`) stays as the control for the console-wide runtime.
- `FormPage.test.ts`: the name fallback case now expects no label, plus a `title` case.
- Two `App.*` tests whose `InternalFormRoute` mock lacked the new export.

Reverse verification, each fix part reverted alone on the committed head: the `hostInConsolePath` branch (6 red, the outside-app and `formsx` controls stay green), the heading chain (4 red), the Cancel button (5 red), the in-app route (3 red). Local runs and gate readings are in the os-dev report on the card.

## Acceptance notes

- `/apps/APP/forms/NAME` shadows the shorthand record redirect for an object literally named `forms` (`forms/ID`), the same way `page/NAME` and `dashboard/NAME` already do.
- Not in scope: the showcase's Log Time targets the task's general edit form (the card's own note, a showcase metadata choice).

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer)
